summary: Selected H1 as a new, provisional, unverified mechanism hypothesis: sufficiently unfavorable interactions between reference-like and variant/length-class RNAs could destabilize a homogeneous dense phase and create a compositionally distinct, RNA-poor internal domain. This does not establish that such a domain is a cavity, or that it explains B's time trend. Algebraically, under the assumed dimensionless regular-solution model g(phi)=phi ln(phi)+(1-phi)ln(1-phi)+chi phi(1-phi), g''=1/phi+1/(1-phi)-2chi; local instability requires chi>1/[2phi(1-phi)], or chi>2 at phi=0.5. No numerical model computation ran, and neither phi nor chi is measured. Three searches supplied only abstract-level general condensate background and a protein-RNA multiphase analogy, not direct RNA-RNA internal-demixing evidence. Data: B's reported statistic rises 0.01381 to 0.08918 from 0 to 24 h while A falls 0.01487 to 0.00446 (initial_measurements.json); endpoint length fractions differ (fraction_dev.json); C04 shows bulk species-dependent partition ratios but not cavity-local composition. DNA frequencies do not determine RNA abundance. C03 confirms the reported t=0 statistic is the mean of object-level ratios, unlike the case brief's pooled-area description; later-time aggregation was not checked. C02's time-only 36/48 h fits are descriptive, with B exponential 0.12072/0.15632 and linear 0.12387/0.16352, no preparation-level interval.

candidates.target: Explain whether the rise in B's image-derived empty-area statistic reflects internal RNA-poor domains, and assess a composition-dependent mechanism for such domains.
known_relations: B reported statistic rises from 0.01381 at 0 h to 0.08918 at 24 h; A falls from 0.01487 to 0.00446 (initial_measurements.json). These condition-level observations do not identify a causal effect of amplification.

C03 verifies at t=0 that the supplied values equal the arithmetic mean of individual object ratios: A 0.01487245 vs summed-area ratio 0.01424891; B 0.01380909 vs 0.01849036. The case brief instead describes a pooled-area ratio. C03 did not check late-time values.

Length-fraction endpoint field means differ: M median 0.0000279, M+L 0.04446, M+S 0.09412 (fraction_dev.json). These results are from one preparation and lack exact mixture fractions, RNA yield, time course, and carryover matching.
C01: reference DNA reads are 94.66%; listed non-reference reads sum to 5.00%; all listed reads total 99.66%. DNA read frequencies are not transcript abundance or active valence.

C04: bulk partition ratios vary across tie-lines. Reference K is about 239-525 on nonzero tie-lines; variant K about 176-9032. Marginal-error propagation gives broad ranges, not confidence intervals; tie-line 0 variant K is undefined because both concentrations are zero. These measurements do not report cavity-local composition or a B time course.

C02: descriptive 36/48 h predictions are A exponential 0.00427/0.00427, B exponential 0.12072/0.15632, and B linear 0.12387/0.16352. There is no preparation-level predictive interval; this time fit does not explain mechanism.

B1-S1_S4 (2021-02-08, abstract only) reports PLP/RRP/RNA ternary demixing: PLP and RNA compete for RRP, and stoichiometry/interaction hierarchy affect engulfment morphology. This is a protein-RNA system, not evidence for demixing between RNA species.
B1-S1_S3 (2023-03-07, abstract only) gives broad associative/segregative transition framing for proteins and nucleic acids without specific RNA-RNA conditions.

B1-S2_S1-S5 (2021-01-25 through 2023-01-25, abstract only) concern protein/crowder phase behavior, PAR versus RNA, protein-RNA multiphase morphology, associative transitions, or general internal condensate architecture. None directly reports RNA-RNA internal demixing in one RNA-rich dense phase.

B1-S3_S1-S5 (2025-01-16 through 2025-05-03, abstract only) concern condensate composition, protein-polyelectrolyte interactions, broad LLPS, multiphase research frontiers, or condensate mechanics. They do not report direct RNA-RNA internal demixing or cavity mapping. Only five abstracts were supplied from 385 hits.

hypotheses.status: selected as a new, case-specific, provisional and unverified mechanism hypothesis; not established as the cause of the observed cavities
hypotheses.statement: If reference-like and variant/length-class RNAs have sufficiently unfavorable mutual interactions within the same dense RNA phase, a local composition fluctuation can cross a demixing instability and form a compositionally distinct, RNA-poor internal domain. Continued transcription or redistribution changing its incidence over time is a separate untested kinetic hypothesis.
hypotheses.derived_consequence: For assumed dimensionless binary regular-solution free energy g(phi)=phi ln(phi)+(1-phi)ln(1-phi)+chi phi(1-phi), differentiation gives g'=ln(phi/(1-phi))+chi(1-2phi), g''=1/phi+1/(1-phi)-2chi. Local instability requires g''<0, hence chi>1/[2phi(1-phi)]; at phi=0.5, chi>2. This is a model-conditional algebraic consequence, not an empirical estimate.
hypotheses.evidence_update: The searches motivate composition-sensitive organization only by analogy and general context. No returned abstract establishes the RNA-RNA premise, an internal RNA-poor cavity, or the kinetic link to B's rise.

gaps.description: No direct evidence that RNA species or length classes demix within the relevant dense phase, and no measurement that a local composition domain is the segmented dark cavity. The available abstracts give general condensate context or protein-RNA analogies only.

C03 verifies arithmetic averaging of object-level ratios at t=0; this differs from the pooled-area definition in case_brief.md. Late-time aggregation has not been checked, limiting quantitative interpretation of population changes.

equations: g(phi)=phi ln(phi)+(1-phi)ln(1-phi)+chi phi(1-phi), 0<phi<1; assumed binary regular-solution model, not fitted.
Local spinodal condition g''<0 gives chi>1/[2phi(1-phi)]. This is not a binodal coexistence condition.
No supplied equation maps local composition or domain geometry to f(t); no kinetic or spatial model is closed.

parameters_ranges.phi: 0<phi<1 by definition; actual local and mean compositions unknown.
parameters_ranges.chi: No empirical range; conditional local-instability threshold is 1/[2phi(1-phi)].

candidates.initial_boundary_conditions: No spatial initial state, boundary conditions, production/transport rates, or local composition measurements supplied. The instability criterion assumes a homogeneous binary mixture with a small perturbation and predicts no time course.
candidates.observation_mapping: A local RNA-poor domain would count as a cavity only if it appears dark under imaging and segmentation. C03 confirms the t=0 statistic is the arithmetic mean of object-level ratios, while case_brief.md states a pooled-area ratio; later-time mapping is unchecked. C04 bulk concentrations are not local cavity concentrations or image area/volume fractions.
alternatives: Population or image-selection effects alter which droplets contribute to the statistic without new within-droplet demixing; available tracking lacks same-droplet cavity-area/state trajectories.
Amplification-associated carryover or another reaction condition changes transcription or morphology; no matched-carryover control is available.
Non-equilibrium production or transport gradients create dark regions within one dense phase without equilibrium RNA-RNA demixing; spatial production and transport are unmeasured.
An environmental change can alter a phase boundary without changing internal molecular arrangement, as reported in a model-protein/crowder abstract; transfer to this RNA system is not established.
predictions: If H1 holds, calibrated species-specific RNA imaging within the same droplets will show a reproducible reference:variant or length-class ratio contrast between cavity interiors and adjacent dense material. At matched total RNA and reaction conditions, changing RNA-class mixture should alter cavity occurrence or morphology. This is a future discriminating prediction, not an observed result.
Population or image-selection effects can change the statistic without requiring a within-droplet RNA-species ratio contrast.
Bulk C04 tie-lines cannot distinguish H1 from these alternatives.
checks: The derivative and spinodal criterion are dimensionless under the stated free-energy convention and depend entirely on the assumed binary regular-solution model.
At phi=0.5 the threshold is chi>2; it diverges as phi approaches 0 or 1 for finite chi.
No compute tool result exists. No fitted parameters, simulated outcomes, or empirical estimates of phi or chi are claimed.
DNA read frequency is not used as RNA abundance; image area fraction is not treated as concentration, volume fraction, or free energy.
C03 checks t=0 only; the case brief and returned data definition differ, and later-time aggregation is unchecked.
B1-S1_S4 is a protein-RNA analogy; S1-S3, S2-S1-S5 and S3-S1-S5 are broad or abstract-only sources. None establishes RNA-RNA internal demixing or cavity identity.
Searches returned 7, 12, and 385 hits respectively, but only five abstracts per search were supplied and reviewed; no conclusion is made about unreviewed hits.
evidence_conflicts: case_brief.md describes total dark area divided by total filled area; C03 shows supplied t=0 values instead match the arithmetic mean of individual object ratios. C03 did not verify later timepoints.
Listed non-reference read fractions sum to 5.00%, not the earlier 4.66% statement; reference plus listed reads total 99.66%, leaving 0.34% unaccounted or attributable to rounding.
untested: Whether B transcripts contain DNA-read variants in corresponding proportions.
Whether the RNA classes have unfavorable mutual mixing under actual transcription conditions.
Whether dark cavities are compositionally distinct phases or result from gradients, population selection, carryover, or image processing.
Whether local domains map to the reported f(t), particularly after t=0.
Whether literature analogies from protein-RNA or protein condensates transfer to this system.
Whether a matched-total-RNA mixture intervention changes within-droplet composition and cavity morphology.
candidates.dissent: Population or measurement selection remains a live alternative. Same-droplet cavity histories are unavailable, f aggregation is checked only at t=0, and the retrieved abstracts do not establish the specific RNA-RNA mechanism. Do not present H1 as confirmed.
candidates.next_task: No further task in this run. The next physical study should test local species composition inside cavities versus adjacent dense material within the same droplets, with controlled RNA-class mixtures at matched total RNA and transcription conditions, matched carryover controls, and parallel object-mean and pooled-area reporting.

final.question_and_reason: Can sufficiently unfavorable interactions between reference-like and variant/length-class RNAs create a local RNA-poor domain inside a transcribing dense RNA droplet? This is a concrete mechanism gap suggested by the endpoint fraction differences, but neither supplied data nor returned abstracts establish it.
final.increment: A case-specific conditional RNA-RNA demixing hypothesis, an algebraic local-instability criterion, and a within-droplet species-ratio prediction, explicitly separated from protein-RNA analogies and population/measurement alternatives.
new_hypotheses: If mutual interactions between two RNA classes exceed the local spinodal threshold at the actual composition, a homogeneous dense phase is locally unstable to composition fluctuations and may form a compositionally distinct RNA-poor domain. Continued production or redistribution causing the observed time rise is a separate unverified hypothesis.
final.actual_derivation_or_computation: Algebraic derivation only. For assumed g(phi)=phi ln(phi)+(1-phi)ln(1-phi)+chi phi(1-phi), differentiation twice gives g''=1/phi+1/(1-phi)-2chi. Requiring g''<0 yields chi>1/[2phi(1-phi)]; at phi=0.5, chi>2. This is dimensionless, conditional on the model, and is a spinodal criterion rather than a binodal calculation. No numerical computation, model fit, simulation, or estimate of phi/chi was run or returned.
final.discriminating_prediction: H1 predicts a reproducible within-droplet difference in reference:variant or length-class RNA ratio between a cavity and adjacent dense material. At matched total RNA and transcription conditions, changing RNA-class mixture should change cavity frequency or morphology. Population/measurement selection can change the aggregate statistic without that within-droplet ratio contrast.
final.evidence_support_conflict_untested: Support is limited to condition-associated time trends (B 0.01381 to 0.08918; A 0.01487 to 0.00446), one-preparation length-fraction endpoints, and bulk C04 phase partitioning. Conflicts and limits: no causal amplification control; DNA read frequencies are not RNA abundance; C04 is not cavity-local; C03 confirms object-mean f only at t=0 despite the case brief's pooled-area definition; only two independent preparations; retrieved literature is abstract-only and does not directly establish RNA-RNA internal demixing or cavity identity.
final.decision: Retain B1-H1 as the selected provisional mechanism hypothesis; do not claim it is confirmed or explains the observation. Current evidence cannot distinguish internal demixing from non-equilibrium gradients, carryover, population selection or measurement effects.
final.dissent: Population or measurement selection remains plausible. Same-droplet cavity histories are unavailable, the later-time f aggregation is unchecked, and the searches did not establish the RNA-RNA or cavity bridge.
final.next_experiment: In a future controlled study, measure species-specific RNA signal inside cavities and in adjacent dense material within the same droplets over time; vary RNA-class mixture at matched total RNA and transcription conditions; include matched carryover controls; and report object-mean and pooled-area statistics in parallel.
final.limitations: The hypothesis uses an assumed binary regular-solution model and omits production, transport, morphology, and measurement noise. No local composition, calibrated image-to-concentration mapping, or independent preparation-level longitudinal data are available. All returned literature is abstract-only; only five abstracts per search were reviewed. No compute tool result exists.
